hearings.business_text: Heard learned counsel for the Decree Holder and the Judgment Debtors on I.A. No. 1, filed under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, seeking recall of the order dated 10.02.2025, whereby this Court had directed issuance of a delivery warrant against JDR Nos. 12 and 13. Upon perusal of the record and the submission of parties, it is evident that the delivery warrant in question was not issued as the property particulars mentioned in the compromise decree do not correspond with the description provided by the DHR in the present execution proceedings. It is a settled principle that execution proceedings must strictly conform to the terms and boundaries of the decree sought to be executed. As per the order dated 10.02.2025 the warrant was not actually issued, therefore, the question of recalling the said order does not arise. Consequently, the application has become infructuous in view of the DHR’s requirement to initiate fresh steps by furnishing a corrected and consistent property schedule, as per the decree. Accordingly, the interlocutory application stands rejected as being infructuous, with liberty to the DHR to provide correct description of the property as per decree. To hear on main petition, by 03.06.2025.
